_comment_application_registration: Self-registration toggle. When false, the /register form is unavailable, the header button reads 'Request access' and links to /view/<redirect-page>, and OIDC auto-provisioning of brand-new users is rejected. Only existing users and accounts created by an admin can log in. Login itself is unaffected. The redirect-page is a page slug operators can edit in the system UI.
_comment_application_registration_passwo: Password /register form toggle (#1026). Subordinate to ngdpbase.application.registration above: that key is the master policy (may ANY path create an account), this one turns off just this mechanism. false → GET and POST /register both 404 and the header button stops advertising it, while other signup paths (magic-link auto-provision, OIDC) still work. Set both to true for stock behaviour; set this false with registration:true for an instance where magic link is the only way to get an account. Default true — existing deploys unchanged.
_comment_application_contact: Optional /contact endpoint (#658, #670). enabled:false → /contact 404. page:'<slug>' → /contact 302-redirects to /view/<slug> (operator-owned content). page:'' → built-in form. recipient accepts two patterns: a single address ('admins@example.com' — distribution list) or an inline CSV ('alice@example.com, bob@example.com') — Nodemailer fans out comma-separated to: headers. recipient:'' → resolves at request time to the first admin user whose email is not the install-default sentinel 'admin@localhost'. Email is never rendered to clients. contact.page === 'contact' is rejected at startup as a redirect loop. Each address in recipient is regex-checked at startup; a malformed segment refuses to start (#670 Phase D). Mail must be enabled (ngdpbase.mail.*) for actual sending. footer.enabled:true → render a 'Contact' link in the page footer when contact is fully available (#670 Phase A); set false to keep /contact reachable without advertising it. persist.enabled:true → append every legitimate POST /contact submission to a JSONL audit log surviving mail failure (#670 Phase C); honeypot/rate-limit submissions are NOT persisted. persist.path:'' → use {instanceDataFolder}/contact-submissions.log; set to an absolute path to override.
_comment_seo: #885/#886 — public-instance discoverability. OFF by default: a private or intranet install must expose nothing extra, and these features assume anonymous visitors are welcome. Turning this on enables OpenGraph/Twitter tags on page views (so shared links unfurl in chat apps) and, once #885 lands, /sitemap.xml. Both require ngdpbase.application.base-url to be set to the real public URL — og:url and sitemap entries must be absolute, and a relative or localhost value is silently ignored by every consumer. Structured data is unaffected: the JSON-LD block ships on every page view regardless (#760/#765).
_comment_trust_proxy: Express 'trust proxy' setting (#861). Default false: req.ip is the direct socket peer. Behind a reverse proxy / Cloudflare Tunnel set to 'loopback' (or a hop count / subnet list) so req.ip reflects X-Forwarded-For and rate limiting / audit see real client IPs. Never true/enabled on directly-reachable instances — X-Forwarded-For is client-spoofable.
_comment_server_tls: #1153 — serve TLS directly. Both must be set and usable, or the instance does NOT quietly fall back to plain HTTP: that is a transport downgrade, where the operator configured TLS, believes traffic is encrypted, and it is in the clear. A broken pair takes the survivable-failure path instead (#1152) — maintenance mode naming the bad file, with /admin and /login reachable so it can be fixed without filesystem access. Neither set is the ordinary case and means plain HTTP with no complaint. An EXPIRED certificate is the deliberate exception: it keeps serving HTTPS and is reported at error level, because falling back would downgrade the transport over a certificate that is merely stale, and a stale certificate is already loudly visible to every client. Note Node does not check expiry itself — the client rejects it — so this is checked explicitly. If something in FRONT of this instance terminates TLS instead, leave these empty and set ngdpbase.server.trust-proxy. See docs/security-posture.md.
_comment_config_secret_keys: Config keys masked on the Admin Configuration screen until an admin with admin-system explicitly reveals one. Deliberately SHORT and a DENY-list, not a pattern match: masking everything that merely LOOKS secret would hide booleans like application.registration.password and auth.password.enabled, and an operator who has to click through those learns to reveal reflexively. A mistake here shows a value to an already-authenticated admin on their own screen — small blast radius, so a short explicit list is the safe default. A read-only admin (admin-read without admin-system) never receives these values at all: they are stripped server-side, not hidden with CSS. Entries need not exist in this file; listing a key that is env-only is harmless and future-proofs it.
_comment_config_env_keys: Config keys OWNED BY THE ENVIRONMENT, and the variable that supplies each (#1089). These are ALWAYS read-only on the Admin Configuration screen — not 'read-only while the variable happens to be set'. A conditional would make the UI the source of truth whenever the variable is unset, which is exactly the ambiguity this removes: a key is owned by one layer, never two. The value shipped for such a key in this file is a BOOT FALLBACK so a fresh install comes up; it is not a setting. To change one, set the variable in .env (root or <FAST_STORAGE>/.env) and restart — nothing in ngdpbase writes .env, by design, with ONE exception: when NGDPBASE_SESSION_SECRET is absent at boot, src/bootstrap-env.ts generates a value and appends it to <FAST_STORAGE>/.env (#1194), because the alternative was signing every session with the public literal shipped below. A config screen that restarts the server is a different feature. Deliberately SHORT: a key earns a place only if the environment must be able to supply it in a deployment where NO config file exists — a fresh headless container boot onto an empty volume is the case that decides it. NOTE application.base-url may equally be set in app-custom-config.json (the install wizard writes it there); it is listed because docker-compose-traefik.yml composes it at deploy time and InstallService names the env var as the alternative for headless installs, so the environment must remain a valid source. Replaces a hardcoded map that used to live in ConfigurationManager.getProperty() where nothing could see it.
_comment_system_principal: #631 — the system principal: the server acting for itself at boot and from timers. IDENTITY is owned by the environment: the value below is the bare env-ref $NGDPBASE_SYSTEM_USER, which THROWS when the variable is unset, so an instance with no named principal refuses to boot rather than acting as a default nobody chose. .env is not reachable from the admin UI, so the name cannot be changed through a form. The name is reserved in the user store: no person can register it. AUTHORITY comes from ngdpbase.system.roles through policy — the same door as any request — and ships as ["admin"]. No roles are ever carried in a job context; the name resolves to these roles at the moment of each permission decision (UserManager.systemSubject).
_comment_session_storage: Session storage directory - high I/O, consider fast storage (SSD)
_comment_http: Global timeout (ms) for ngdpbase's own outbound HTTP fetches (NCM image fetch #728, URL import). Does NOT override third-party clients that manage their own timeouts (Elasticsearch, OTLP).
_comment_application_organization: Identity of THIS install (#617). The org JSON-LD file at <storagedir>/<file> is the single source of truth — name, url, address, etc. live IN THE FILE, not in config. Install completion tracked via INSTANCE_DATA_FOLDER/.install-complete (not config).
_comment_application_persons: Person records storage (#617). One file per person under storagedir.
_comment_application_roles: OrganizationRole records storage (#617 follow-up). One file per (organization, namedPosition) pair under storagedir, named <namedPosition>.json. Snapshot at create time from the catalog at ngdpbase.roles.definitions.
_comment_page_index: Page index file - used by VersioningFileProvider for fast lookups (high I/O, consider fast storage)
_comment_page_delete: Days a soft-deleted page stays restorable before it is purged along with its version history (#947). Set 0 to keep deleted pages forever.
_comment_page_chrome: Pages excluded from tab injection or footer rendering
_comment_share: Share links (#842): anonymous capability-token access to keyword-scoped content. Keys approved by operator 2026-07-16.
_comment_capture: Bookmarklet capture (#881): optional feature, disabled by default — /capture routes 404 unless enabled per instance. default-page supports {date} and {username} tokens.
_comment_ncm_image: ngdp Compatible Markdown embedded-image rule (#728 §2.2). Size cap reuses ngdpbase.attachment.maxsize; the accepted raster set is a fixed NCM allowlist (jpeg/png/gif/webp — SVG/RAW excluded, not configurable: NCM tightens, never loosens). ad-deny-list: hosts/host+path substrings whose images are dropped (not attached); matched case-insensitively against the URL.
_comment_ncm_table: ngdp Compatible Markdown table up-convert (#728 §2.1, NCM v2). On normalization, GFM pipe tables are rewritten to the JSPWiki styled form (||header||/|cell|) wrapped in these style blocks, giving imported tables fit/border/zebra/hover + client-side sorting. Order is preserved; set to [] to up-convert the table syntax with no style wrapper.
_comment_legacy_database_files: LEGACY: These properties are not used in code - kept for reference only
_comment_user_storage: User authentication and storage configuration (ALL LOWERCASE)
_comment_user_security_defaultpassword: Password given to the bootstrap 'admin' account, applied ONLY on the boot that finds an empty user store. Ships as 'admin123' so a fresh install comes up unattended and the setup wizard is reachable. Change it on first login — the startup banner warns until you do. To supply it from the environment instead, set this key to "$NGDPBASE_ADMIN_PASSWORD" in app-custom-config.json and put the value in .env; a bare $VAR ref is strict, so an unset variable stops the boot rather than quietly falling back. Read inside createDefaultAdmin(), never at startup, so an instance that already has an admin never resolves it.
_comment_auth: Authentication provider chain — ngdpbase.auth.required-factors is an ordered list of provider IDs that must be satisfied for login (e.g. ['password'] or ['password','totp'] for MFA)
_comment_auth_throttle: Login throttling (#1044) — failed password attempts are counted per username AND per client IP; a success clears the count. Locks always EXPIRE: a permanent lock on a known username like admin would be a denial-of-service vector against the operator. Consecutive lockouts double the wait, capped by max-lock-minutes.
_comment_mail: Email transport — used by magic-link auth, notifications, and server alerts. See docs/admin/email-setup.md
_comment_mail_smtp: SMTP settings (provider='smtp'). Works with any relay: Gmail, Resend, SendGrid, SES, self-hosted. smtp.from overrides mail.from and allows display names.
_comment_mail_anti_spam: Anti-spam defenses for mail-bearing public forms (#670 Phase E). Today only /contact uses these; future mail-bearing public forms (re-enabled /register, magic-link request, etc.) should read the same flags. honeypot.enabled:false → don't silently drop submissions where the hidden _website field was filled. rate-limit.enabled:false → don't 429 any submission, regardless of frequency. max-submissions / window-minutes tune the rate limit budget per source IP.
_comment_magic_link: Magic link (passwordless) authentication — requires ngdpbase.mail.enabled:true. Any transport works: provider:'smtp' to actually send, provider:'console' to print the link to the server log for local testing. Verify-link host is derived from ngdpbase.application.base-url (#642); the provider refuses to register unless that key is set explicitly, because a token in a URL is a credential and must not point at the localhost default. Tokens are held in memory, so a restart invalidates every outstanding link.
_comment_magic_link_auto_provision: Magic-link registration (#1026). false (default) → a link is only ever sent to an address that already has an account; an unknown address is answered identically but no mail is sent, which is what prevents user enumeration. true → an unknown address also receives a link, and the account is created when that link is VERIFIED, not when it is requested — so an address nobody controls never becomes an account. Subordinate to ngdpbase.application.registration: with the master policy false, this key does nothing (same precedence OIDC auto-provisioning uses). Accounts created this way are isExternal, meaning an empty password hash that no password can match — magic link is structurally their only way in. default-role is the role they receive; an unknown role name falls back to 'reader' with a warning rather than minting a more privileged account than intended. Open signup sends mail to caller-supplied addresses, so keep ngdpbase.mail.rate-limit.* enabled.
_comment_magic_link_binding: #1022: bind a magic link to the browser that requested it. Observability is unconditional — every redemption is recorded via AuditManager with IP, User-Agent and whether the redeeming browser matched. This flag adds ENFORCEMENT, and defaults false on purpose: request-on-laptop/open-on-phone is the common real flow, and refusing it would be worse than the bearer-token risk it mitigates. Turn on only where every user redeems on the requesting device.
_comment_chrome: Site chrome page resolution (#952). Names the page supplying the left menu / footer. EMPTY means fall back to the legacy slug convention ('left-menu-content' shadowing 'LeftMenu', 'footer-content' shadowing 'Footer') — kept so upgrades do not change behaviour on instances relying on it. Set explicitly (a domain addon can via domainDefaults) to make the choice visible; when set it is authoritative and a missing page is reported rather than silently substituted.
_comment_agent_token: User-delegated agent API tokens (#946) — any user mints short-lived bearer credentials for their own agents. A token can never exceed its owner's live permissions, and admin-* scopes are refused outright. Off by default. sweep-interval-seconds drives a background sweep that flushes buffered lastUsedAt stamps and purges records dead longer than retention-days; it is unrelated to the ngdpbase.features.maintenance.* keys, which are maintenance MODE. retention-days and max-per-user accept 0 (purge as soon as dead / allow none); TTL and interval keys require at least 1. retention-days is 1 rather than 30 because the lifecycle is audited (#1111): token.mint and token.revoke outlive the record, so the store keeps dead credentials only long enough for the admin list to show what happened to a token yesterday, not as a stand-in audit trail. The store is never copied aside — see #1110.
_comment_google_oidc: Google OIDC ('Sign in with Google') — see jwilleke/ngdpbase#447. Set credentials in app-custom-config.json (never commit secrets).
_comment_cloudflare_access: Cloudflare Access JWT trust (#649) — verifies Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion header on every request. team-domain + application-aud must be set in app-custom-config.json before enabling. group-map maps CF group names (from JWT identity.groups) to ngdpbase role names; CF groups with no mapping are ignored (user gets default-role only).
_comment_schema_types: JSON-LD @type per system-category (#791) — operator-controllable schema.org subtypes. articleToPageJsonLd consults this map at render time; categories not listed fall through to 'Article'. Shipped Article-subtype defaults: documentation/developer → TechArticle, journal → BlogPosting (no-op until `journal` is registered as a system-category per EPIC #790). Operators may add Article-family or non-Article (e.g. FAQPage) types per deployment in app-custom-config.json. See docs/schemas.md § Per-category JSON-LD @type.
_comment_password_auth: Password (local) authentication — set false to hide the password form when Google OIDC is the only desired login method
_comment_user_external: Default isExternal for newly provisioned users. false = local account with password. OIDC auto-provision overrides to true.
_comment_theme: Theme settings — ngdpbase.theme.active is the folder name under themes/; ngdpbase.theme.directory is the instance themes root (also the #443 addon-theme deploy target); ngdpbase.theme.defaults.mode is the default light/dark mode for new users
_comment_directories: LEGACY: Directory settings - use provider-specific configs instead (e.g., ngdpbase.page.provider.filesystem.storagedir)
_comment_addons: Add-on system configuration - individual add-ons configured under ngdpbase.addons.<name>
_comment_audit_chain_witness: #1138 — off-box witness for the audit chain head. The chain detects alteration and deletion but NOT truncation of the tail: removing records from the end breaks no link, and that is the attack an intruder actually wants. It cannot be fixed locally — an attacker who owns the machine owns anything the machine wrote locally, including a head stored beside the log — so the head has to leave the box or it is not evidence. Set destination to a path OUTSIDE this machine's trust boundary: a network mount, an append-only share, a write-once store. Empty means no witness is published, and truncation stays undetectable. This code takes no view on whether your destination is genuinely off-box and never claims it is: nothing here can verify that a path leaves the machine, and asserting so would repeat the durable defect #1148 removed. It reports where it published and when, and you state what that destination is. interval-minutes is the SECURITY PARAMETER, not a performance knob — the gap between publications is the window an attacker can truncate within. See docs/security-posture.md D13, D20 and D21.
_comment_audit_events: #1200/#1201 (epic #1208) — the audit event registry and vocabulary, keyed by event. Names are {target}-{action}, hyphens only, matching the permission slug where the action is the one the permission authorizes; the code lists the same names once in src/utils/auditEventNames.ts and a test holds the two equal. Events are actions taken; permissions are authority; neither carries the other's fields. on-failure: what happens when the record cannot be written — refuse (the action must not complete unless the record does; the write is flushed to the device first) or continue (the action proceeds, the lost record is counted and surfaced). How important an event is lives on each record as severity; this field is only failure handling (#1218). enabled: whether the emitter fires; omitted means true; false is a decision on the record. description: one line, shown in the admin filter and the documented table. A map, not an array, so app-custom-config.json overrides one entry and null removes one. Configuration is authoritative: code emits what this names and honours the on-failure rule it declares; npm run lint:audit fails when the two disagree. See docs/audit-posture.md.

_comment_security_egress: #1133 — the outbound address boundary. Two CIDR lists, IPv4 and IPv6, evaluated against the address the server actually resolved and connected to, on every redirect hop. NOT a URL list: a URL check cannot be the boundary, because a redirect sends the request somewhere the original URL never named and a name can resolve differently between validation and connection. Loopback, link-local (which covers 169.254.169.254), multicast and Teredo are the MECHANISM and are refused on every profile — no allow entry reaches them, because an editor on your LAN can already reach the LAN but cannot reach 127.0.0.1 on the server. RFC1918, CGNAT and IPv6 unique-local are POLICY: denied by default and openable here, so a home instance can permit its own segment with '192.168.68.0/24' without also permitting 10.0.0.0/8 and in-cluster space. Overlap between the lists is normal and resolves by LONGEST PREFIX — the routing convention, used because the values are routes — with explicit entries beating the built-in defaults at equal length. The lists are reconciled at boot and NOTHING stops the boot (#1144): an allow entry reaching the mechanism is unsatisfiable and dropped, and a range appearing verbatim in both is a prefix-length tie the DENY wins — the operator's stricter statement survives. A range that does not parse as CIDR is the one case with no safe silent resolution, because a malformed deny rule means the restriction was never applied; it is reported loudly and #1152 will make it block serving.
_comment_security_posture: #1145 — the security posture: which settings make up what this instance guarantees, presented as one subject. A VIEW, not a resolution layer — every entry is an ordinary key with its own shipped default, read by live code, and the posture changes no value on its own. That is also why removing an entry is safe: the key keeps whatever it is set to and the code keeps reading it, it only stops being displayed. A MAP keyed by the ingredient rather than groups holding arrays, because a plain array is replaced wholesale on merge and an operator adding one entry would silently drop the rest; a map merges per entry, and an entry set to null removes a shipped one. 'restart' says whether a change takes effect only after a restart, which is written down rather than compared against the running process: a boot snapshot misreports the settings whose consumers re-read live (LoginThrottle, SimpleRateLimiter), and instrumenting every subsystem to derive a flag a maintainer can simply state is the wrong trade. Keys named in ngdpbase.config.secret-keys are reported as set but never rendered. See docs/security-posture.md.
_comment_audit_on_failure: #1118 — what happens when auditing is configured but the provider cannot be used. 'refuse-boot' names the provider and the cause and refuses to finish booting: since #1152 the instance stays RUNNING and serves the maintenance page, keeping /admin and /login reachable so the provider can be repaired without filesystem access. It is blocking, not fatal — the process does not exit, because exiting would leave an operator with no route back except the disk; 'continue' falls back to the inert provider and marks the instance DEGRADED, reported by AuditManager.getAuditPosture() and shown as a banner on the admin dashboard. The value here IS the effective policy — #1144 removed the profile preset that could otherwise have supplied a different default, so nothing is inferred. Set 'refuse-boot' where the instance must not serve without an audit trail; docs/security-posture.md carries the recommended value sets. NOTE this is NOT the same as turning auditing off: an operator who wants no auditing sets ngdpbase.audit.enabled false or selects nullauditprovider, which is a decision on the record and is not degraded.
_comment_audit_scaffolds: #1118 — DatabaseAuditProvider and CloudAuditProvider are SCAFFOLDS. Their source is a list of TODOs and both refuse at initialize(). Their configuration keys were removed rather than left here: a populated connectionstring reads as a working feature, and selecting one previously produced an instance that silently audited nowhere. Restore these keys in the same change that implements the provider, not before.
_comment_markup_render_tags: Fenced code block language tags the system recognises. Tags not in this list are flagged as unknown on page save. 'wiki' is intentionally absent — it has no special meaning here.
_comment_spam_filters: Spam filter configuration. Heuristic link/image/word limits on page content. Ships DISABLED. The comment that used to sit here was labelled security_filters and described SecurityFilter, which starts nine keys further down — the text now lives above the keys it documents.
_comment_security_filters: Security filter configuration. Strips dangerous markup from RENDERED page HTML (phase: html). Ships DISABLED: on a wiki whose authors are trusted, raw HTML in a page is a feature, and enabling this removes it. Enable it on any instance whose authors are strangers — a public demo, an open-registration site — because markdown permits raw HTML by design and nothing else stops a page author injecting script. It was unusable before #1032: prevent-xss entity-encoded the whole rendered document, so every page displayed as visible HTML source, and the tag allow-list omitted tables, code blocks and blockquotes. Both fixed; allowed-tags/allowed-attributes below now ADD to a built-in baseline covering everything ngdpbase renders, rather than replacing it.

_comment_demo: Demo addon (#1029) — content for a PUBLIC DEMO instance: Welcome / Sandbox / Feature Tour pages, and (once #1029 lands the admin-read permission) a read-only demo-admin role letting visitors open the admin dashboard without being able to change anything. Leave false on any real install: enabling it seeds demo pages that invite strangers to edit, and publishes credentials on the Welcome page. It exists as an addon so that content ships ONLY to instances that opt in — these pages previously lived in core required-pages/ and were therefore offered to every deployment.
_comment_demo_admin_account: Shared read-only admin account seeded by the demo addon when it is enabled, so that enabling the addon is the whole setup and the credentials published on the Welcome page cannot drift from reality. Seeded once and never overwritten — rotate the password through /admin/users/admindemo/edit and the change survives restarts. The account holds only demo-admin (read-only dashboard) and is created with passwordLocked, so a visitor who logs in with the published password cannot change it and lock everyone else out; an administrator still can. Inert unless ngdpbase.addons.demo.enabled is true.
_comment_demo_admin_password: Password for the shared read-only demo account. Ships as the well-known 'admin123' ON PURPOSE: it is printed on the demo Welcome page, so its value is not a secret and shipping it gives away nothing the page does not already say. Safety comes from elsewhere — the account holds only admin-read (it cannot change anything) and is created with profileLocked, so no visitor can take it over by changing its password or email. Contrast ngdpbase.user.security.defaultpassword, which is a real secret guarding admin-system and therefore ships no default at all. Shipping a value here is what keeps enabling the addon the WHOLE setup, with no per-deployment manual step. Override with a literal or the NGDPBASE_DEMO_ADMIN_PASSWORD env-ref if you run a demo whose login you do not publish.

_comment_permissions: Canonical permission registry. Format: {target}-{action}. Target-first, hyphen-separated (URL-safe, matches the 'permissions' array in role definitions). Each entry: description, icon (Font Awesome name), color (hex). The key itself is the permission name.

_comment_roles: #713 — Role definitions serve TWO purposes that must stay in sync: (1) inline `permissions[]` arrays are read by ConfigAccessorPlugin to render the role×permission matrix on the Roles/Permissions required-pages (display only). (2) Runtime authorization decisions go through PolicyEvaluator.evaluateAccess(), which reads `ngdpbase.access.policies` below — NOT the inline arrays. Keep the two lists matched: editing one without the other introduces display-vs-enforcement drift. (ALL LOWERCASE)
